title: platform-standup-2026-03-20
content:
Date: 2026-03-20
Attendees: Priya Kapoor (owner), Marcus Patel, Sofia Gonzalez, Liam O'Connor, Ava Nguyen, Ben Cho (notes)

Quick notes / agenda
- 1) Control plane health + rollout status
- 2) Routing layer: fallbacks and region affinity work
- 3) Auth and quotas: rate limit enforcement bug + migration plan
- 4) Ops/Incidents and on-call handoff
- 5) Action items and blockers

1) Control plane
- Update: Canary rollout for the new control-plane actor scheduler completed to 50% of traffic last night. Metrics: median API start time down ~12% for warm requests, 95th still noisy (investigating tail behavior).
- Work in progress: Marcus is instrumenting per-tenant scheduling traces to correlate long tail with specific tenant routing rules (JIRA-PLT-4821). Expect initial dashboards by EOD Thu.
- Notes: two old feature flags were left enabled for a subset of dedicated customers; we toggled them off during the rollout to reduce scheduling churn.

2) Routing
- Update: Region-affinity policy merged to staging (PR #214). Staging load tests show correct fallback to secondary region when primary capacity is exceeded.
- Action: Sofia to run a synthetic test that simulates multi-tenant spike + 20% capacity drain to validate cross-region latency impact. Target: Friday morning load window.
- Open issue: sticky session behavior for streaming responses not preserved across fallback path; identified root cause in our session-key hashing. Short-term fix: preserve kv-cache id during reroute. Ticket: JIRA-PLT-4798.

3) Auth and quotas
- Incident: We observed a quota enforcement regression yesterday where some users bypassed burst limits due to race between token-creation and quota-cache refresh. Impact: ~1200 requests over burst threshold across two customers; no data exfiltration.
- Root cause: race in quota-cache invalidation when API keys are rotated.
- Mitigation: Ava deployed a hotfix that adds a short TTL-based guard and forces quota cache invalidation on key rotate. Patch deployed to prod and rolled back for one tenant for verification.
- Next: implement stronger transactional invalidation and add unit tests. Owner: Ava. ETA: 2026-03-27.

4) Quotas (policy + billing alignment)
- Update: Prototype of usage-reporting pipeline for per-route quota reconciliation is in review. This will enable daily reconciliation with billing to avoid surprises for customers using dedicated pools.
- Need decision: Do we auto-honor overages for a 24h window or fail-fast? Product asked for a conservative approach (fail-fast + soft alerts). Meeting with Product scheduled Thursday.

5) Ops / incidents / on-call
- On-call note: Liam will be primary for next rotation (2026-03-21 -> 2026-03-28). Weekend coverage confirmed by Marcus.
- Recent incident postmortem draft linked in Slack; Ben to circulate final doc by Friday.

Blockers
- Telemetry: We need per-tenant trace sampling to be enabled in prod without high cardinality explosion. Marcus to propose sampling plan today; blocker for scheduling traces.
- Routing sticky sessions: short-term fix in progress but needs QA signoff from QA team before can go to prod.
- Billing decision on quota overages blocks final rollout of the reconciliation pipeline.

Action items (owners + ETA)
- Marcus: Finish per-tenant scheduling traces + dashboard (ETA: 2026-03-21).
- Sofia: Run cross-region spike tests and share results (ETA: 2026-03-21 AM).
- Ava: Implement transactional quota-cache invalidation + tests (ETA: 2026-03-27).
- Priya: Coordinate product meeting for billing/overages policy and capture decision (ETA: 2026-03-23).
- Ben: Finalize incident postmortem and share with SRE/product (ETA: 2026-03-22).

Decisions
- Canary rollout will proceed to 100% in stages once per-tenant trace dashboards do not show unexplained tail latencies.
- Billing policy: hold proposed fail-fast approach for discussion; no auto-honor until product sign-off.

References / links
- JIRA-PLT-4821: per-tenant scheduling traces
- JIRA-PLT-4798: routing fallback sticky-session bug
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform-runtime/pull/214
- Slack: #eng-platform (see thread: "control-plane canary 3")

Notes to self / loose thoughts
- Consider adding a lightweight tenant-level synthetic that runs every 30m to exercise routing fallbacks; could help detect regressions earlier.
- Revisit session-key hashing design after sticky-session fix is stable.

Next standup: 2026-03-23 (weekly cadence)
